reason: A: the headline wraps as 'Garden-fresh / fizz', leaving 'fizz' alone on the second line, but it stays large and dominant and the headline, subhead and CTA sit together as one tightly spaced group. B: the headline fits on one line but is smaller and sits in an awkward gap, with a big space before the subhead and then the subhead jammed against the CTA, so the vertical rhythm is uneven. Both leave about 80px of empty space at the bottom, crowd the SOLSTICE logo and bottle into the decorative circles at the top, and set the subhead at a small size for this format.

The two candidates use the same layout. The product bag fills the canvas width well, but in both the bottom third is mostly empty beside a gold circle that has been cropped at the corner, so the weight sits too high. A breaks the headline to leave 'fizz' alone on the second line, and the larger two-line block crowds the CTA, with only about 20px between them. B keeps the headline on one line with even space above and below, but it nearly runs into the side edges with only about 28px of margin.

The two layouts are almost identical, and both have the same problems. The white logo band stops abruptly at x≈518 and leaves a strange navy strip above it. The divider rule is moved up beside the CTA, where it floats with no purpose. The body copy is jammed right under the headline and sits off the headline's centre axis, close to the bottom edge. The CTA is pushed out to the right, so the block looks like a fragment and the reading order is broken. The only difference is the logo: A's is a little larger and closer to the original's proportion, while B's is shrunk and looks weaker inside the white band.

A and B look pixel-identical, and both have the same problems. The 'LONGEST DAY SALE' ribbon is pushed against the bottom-left edge and nearly cut off. The can is shrunk to an unreadable thumbnail. The legal copy is about as big as the CTA, wraps in three ragged lines that run into the right edge, and sits on the busy dotted background. The logo, ribbon and can are scattered with no shared baseline or alignment.

The two layouts are almost identical. In both, the headline breaks one word per line ('Make / the / longest / day / last') and takes up most of the skyscraper, which swamps everything else. The CTA, the '25% off' line and the legal text are crammed into the bottom fifth: the legal copy is jammed under the button and against the bottom edge, and the decorative circles are gone. A's sun icon and SOLSTICE wordmark are slightly larger and easier to read, while B's logo has shrunk to an almost illegible speck above the ribbon. That makes A marginally less bad on brand.

A: the headline wraps to four ragged lines and starts only about 20px from the top edge, so the top is cramped and the headline almost runs into the bottom row. B: the headline sets in three lines with more even top and bottom margins and better balance, though the 'botanicals and a' break leaves 'a' dangling at the end of a line. In both, the italic subline is tiny and low-contrast, and it is pushed into a cramped left-aligned bottom row next to the CTA, which breaks the original's centered axis.

Both share the same flaws: the phone illustration is jammed against the top-left edge and cropped, the top-right quadrant and the bottom ~120px are dead space, the subhead is indented at x≈105 on no clear axis, and the tilted 'ONLINE ONLY' badge sits awkwardly beside the CTA. A's one-line headline spans the width and shares a right edge with the subhead, so the stack at least reads as one block. B's two-line headline is left-aligned at x≈48 but the subhead starts at x≈105 and is wider than the headline, so neither its left nor right edges line up, and the headline crowds right up to the subhead.

Both use the same cramped leaderboard layout. The tagline is squeezed into a narrow 5-line italic column, and 'SOLSTICE PRESENTS' is shrunk to illegible size and moved below the headline, which breaks the reading order. The RSVP button is just one more pill among the three badges, so the CTA is buried. The placeholder for the missing partner asset is jammed under the logo. A keeps the sun icon on the Solstice logo; B appears to lose it and shows a bigger placeholder box, so A is very slightly better.

The two candidates look pixel-identical, so they share the same flaws. The RSVP Free CTA has been shrunk into the badge row and reads as a fourth tag rather than the main action. A stray dark bar left over from the partner asset trails the TASTINGS pill, the can icon is crammed into the middle, and the logo is pushed to the right edge, so the reading order is scattered.

Both use the same jumbled leaderboard layout. The RSVP button has shrunk to a pill the same size as the Free Entry, All Ages and Tastings tags, so the CTA is buried. The logo is clipped against the left edge in both. A's logo is noticeably oversized and competes with the headline, and B's smaller logo is slightly better proportioned, so B wins by a hair.

Both 320×50 banners have the same layout. There is also wasted space above the quote mark, and the logo sits on its own, close to the circle's left edge. The only difference is the logo: A keeps it at a legible size, while B shrinks it to a tiny, harder-to-read mark, so A is slightly better.

A and B look pixel-identical: both are close to a uniform scale-down of the square onto the 300x250 canvas, not a real rearrangement. In both, the 'THE GROVE TASTING TEAM' attribution, the bottom-left logo and the 'SOLSTICE' can label shrink to a few pixels and can't be read. The can also sits too close to the bottom edge, and the left-column quote leaves a dead band under the attribution.

The two candidates are effectively the same layout. The only visible difference is that B's SOLSTICE logo is a few pixels narrower. Both have the same flaws: the purple circle is now fully on the canvas and sits right under the quote text instead of bleeding off the left edge as in the original. There is a large empty band above the quote mark. The product can stays small and pushed right inside an oversized maroon circle, leaving the lower-left nearly empty apart from the tiny logo.

Both candidates are essentially the same proportional shrink, not a rearrangement. In each, the decorative circles are now oversized for the canvas. The right circle runs up behind the end of the quote and the attribution, and the left circle sits behind the start of the quote, so there are no clean background zones left. The SOLSTICE logo wordmark in the bottom-left corner and the label on the product can are too small to read, and the attribution line is borderline. A's wordmark is very slightly larger, but the two are practically identical.

Both are the same near-copy: the photo panel no longer bleeds to the canvas edges and sits inside thin dark strips at the top and bottom, which looks like a letterboxed mistake. The left column also floats in extra vertical space, and the SAVE 15% badge still drifts away from both the logo and the headline. B is slightly better only because it breaks the headline as 'Your coffee, / on repeat', where A leaves the weak, awkward wrap 'on / repeat'.

The two candidates look pixel-identical: a sensible left-to-right banner with logo, a large one-line headline, then the shoe in its lime circle at the right. Both share the same flaws. 'Full review inside.' is broken into a tiny three-line stack jammed beside the circle, the 'NEW VIDEO' pill is shrunk to near-illegible size and wedged under the logo, and the shoe circle is crushed against the right edge with very little margin.

The two candidates look pixel-identical. Both shrink the plan cards until the MONTHLY/YEARLY/FAMILY labels and the 'per month' text can't be read, and they put the cards in the wrong order (6, 80, 48), so the highlighted yearly plan is no longer in the middle. Both also jam the subhead and the legal text into a cramped block against the right edge, where the fine print is almost as big as the supporting copy, so the hierarchy breaks down.

A and B look pixel-identical at this banner size, so they share the same flaws. The plan cards are out of order (6, 80, then the dark 48 card, where the original goes Monthly, Yearly, Family), so the featured Yearly plan gets pushed to the edge. The card labels, 'per month' text, subhead and legal line are all far too small to read. The left column is cramped next to the headline, though the headline and orange CTA do read clearly and the brand survives.

Both use the same broken layout. The one-word-per-line headline takes up about 60% of the skyscraper, so the plan cards shrink to tiny tiles with unreadable labels. The cards are also out of order (Monthly, Family, Yearly instead of Monthly, Yearly, Family), and the CTA comes before the plans and the subhead. A is worse because its pacewell logo is shrunk to an illegible speck. B keeps the logo a readable size, though it sits cramped against the headline.

Both use the same layout. In both, the green circle now sits behind the can and crowds it, and the subhead sits too close to the CTA button. A breaks the headline so that 'fizz' is left alone on the second line, but its text block reads as one evenly spaced group. B keeps the headline on one line but runs it almost to the canvas edges, and spacing is uneven: there is a large gap between the headline and the subhead, then cramped spacing between the subhead and the CTA, which weakens the grouping.

A: the headline is oversized and breaks onto two lines, leaving 'fizz' alone on the second line. It sits almost against the top edge and is jammed onto the CTA, and it crowds out the can. The legal text is unreadably small, sits right against the CTA and wraps to leave 'details.' alone on its own line. B: the headline fits on one line and has room to breathe, which gives a clearer order from headline to CTA. It still shares A's flaws: the legal line is tiny and badly wrapped, the CTA is pushed off-centre to the right, the logo sits on the teal circle, and the gap between the headline and the CTA feels arbitrary.

The two candidates use the same weak leaderboard layout. In both, the four-line headline fills the strip, the body copy is a narrow, hard-to-read column, 'Ships late June' wraps into a ragged three-word stack, and the legal text is unreadably small at this height. The Reserve a Case button is also tiny and pushed into the top-right corner, where it competes with the legal block. In A the logo is broken: the sun icon has drifted to the right edge of the dark panel, away from a tiny 'SOLSTICE' wordmark. B keeps the sun centred above a larger, legible wordmark, so its brand mark survives better, though it is still cramped.

A and B look the same. In both, the dark header bar doesn't span the canvas: there's a strip of cream on the left and a wider one on the right, so it reads as a misplaced block rather than a full-bleed header. Both also leave a large dead gap between the 'Limited Summer Release' eyebrow and the headline. 'Ships late June' floats about 90px below the CTA, so it's separated from the button it belongs to, and the legal text at the bottom is tiny and hard to read.

The two layouts are the same except for the logo. In both, the white logo band stops short of the right edge, leaving a dark gap. The body copy sits jammed under the headline. The orange divider has drifted down onto the top edge of the CTA button. The bottom quarter of the canvas is empty. In A the logo is close to the original's proportion (about a quarter of the width) and has some breathing room in its band. In B the logo is blown up to about half the width and jammed against the edges of the white band, so it competes with the headline and looks cramped.

Both use the same weak four-column 728x90 layout. The six-line headline is crammed into three dense lines with no breathing room, and the body copy is shrunk into a five-line block of roughly 7px text that you can't read at banner size. The 'Reserve a Case' button and 'Ships late June' are tiny and jammed against the right edge, 'LIMITED SUMMER RELEASE' is cut off from the headline it introduces, and the orange divider is gone. The only difference is the logo: A's is larger and reads better inside the white panel, while B's is shrunk to a small mark lost in empty white space, so A is marginally better.

Both candidates take the tall portrait stack, shrink it, and drop it into the middle of a 320x50 strip instead of rearranging it as a left-to-right banner. The headline, body copy and 'Reserve a Case' button are microscopic and unreadable, and wide empty navy panels fill both sides. A at least keeps the logo visible in the white band. In B the white band looks empty with no logo, and the headline stack has an odd gap, so B is slightly worse.

At this size I can't see any difference between the two; both are the same failed 320x50 layout. In both, the headline is squeezed into four lines that fill the whole height, the SOLSTICE logo and dark brand header are gone, and the body copy and legal text are a few pixels tall and unreadable. The CTA is a tiny pill crowded under the body copy, and the legal text takes up as much space as the message, so the hierarchy collapses.

Both candidates share the same problems. The 'LIMITED SUMMER RELEASE' eyebrow has dropped below the headline and is shrunk to unreadable micro-text. The orange divider has been moved under the legal text at the bottom, where it serves no purpose. The SOLSTICE logo is tiny, and the body copy is so large that it competes with the headline. A's four-line headline wrap makes 'Small-Batch' run almost edge to edge with no side margin. B's three-line wrap leaves better side margins but opens up an awkward empty band above the headline.

Both use the same cramped leaderboard layout. The legal text is set at an unreadable size and jammed into a block right beside the CTA, the subcopy sits against the top and right edges, the bottle is shrunk until its label can't be read, and the tilted ribbon crowds the logo. A also has a broken wordmark: it reads 'SOLST CE' with a gap under the sun icon. B's 'SOLSTICE' is intact, so B wins narrowly.

The two layouts are almost identical and share the same flaws. The headline is squeezed into three tight lines that fill the full banner height. The legal fine print sits in a narrow column on the far right, wraps into six lines and is almost as large as the offer copy, so it competes with the CTA. The tilted sale ribbon is wedged into the bottom-left corner, and the bottle is tiny. B keeps the SOLSTICE logo at a readable size above the ribbon. A shrinks the logo to an illegible speck, which hurts the brand, so B is slightly better.

The two are almost identical. Both break the headline into five one-word lines, set the legal fine print at nearly the size of the subhead, and pack the subhead, CTA and legal text into the bottom third, with the legal text tight against the bottom edge, while the bottle area above has generous space. A's SOLSTICE wordmark at the top is a little smaller and harder to read than B's, so B keeps the brand slightly better.

The two are nearly identical 320x50 banners, and both are broken in the same ways. The legal fine print gets the prime left slot at almost body-copy size, where the product thumbnail is cramped. The 'Longest Day Sale' ribbon has shrunk to an unreadable sliver under the headline. A's logo is just a tiny sun icon with no readable wordmark. B at least shows the SOLSTICE wordmark in the left cluster, so the brand survives slightly better, but the hierarchy and the fine-print problems are the same.

The two banners are nearly identical. In both, the legal fine print sits leftmost, fills two or three lines and is about as large as the subhead, so it is the first thing the eye reads. The 'Longest Day Sale' ribbon is shrunk to an unreadable sliver that overlaps the phone, and the phone itself is a tiny smudge. The logo is a speck in the top-left corner, crowded against the legal text. B's SOLSTICE wordmark is slightly more visible, so B is marginally less bad on brand.

The two layouts are almost the same, and both have the same problems. The two badges ('Back by demand', 'Summer only') sit stranded below the CTA, which puts the reading order out of sequence. The subhead is tiny, and large dead gaps sit above and below the phone. A breaks the headline into three lines and leaves 'back' alone on the last line. B keeps the headline to two lines, which reads better, but it runs almost to the right edge and starts slightly left of the other elements' left edge.

Both have the same broken lower half. The left edges are ragged: the subhead starts at about x70, the chips at x65 and x106, and the legal line at x87. The Shop Flavours CTA floats to the right with no anchor, the three chips are staggered at random, and there is dead space at the bottom. A at least lines up the logo and the three-line headline on one left edge. B pushes the headline out to x38, so the logo, headline and subhead each start at a different point, and it leaves a large empty gap between the headline and the subhead.

The two candidates share the same flawed right cluster. The Try It button overlaps the bottom of the product circle, and 'Out now.' has been pulled away from the headline and stuck beside the button, so it reads as a stray label. All the weight sits on the right while the left is mostly empty. A's two-line headline is a sensible size and leaves a gap before the circle. B's one-line headline runs almost into the circle, which makes the layout look cramped and less intentional.

The two layouts are almost identical and share the same flaws. The RSVP CTA has shrunk to the size of the FREE ENTRY/ALL AGES/TASTINGS pills, so the action is buried. 'Sessions' is jammed near the bottom edge, and the italic subhead is squeezed between the headline and the date. The 'Reserve a spot' line and the legal text are tiny, and the placeholder image box and the small product can float in the right corner. B is slightly worse because its SOLSTICE wordmark is damaged: it reads as 'SOLST CE', with a glyph missing or covered, which breaks the brand.

The two layouts are almost identical, and both are cramped. The fine print, the subcopy and the date/venue lines are illegibly small at this banner height. The RSVP button is no bigger than the FREE ENTRY, ALL AGES and TASTINGS badges, so it gets lost among them. The product can and the placeholder image are jammed into a dense right-hand cluster, and 'SOLSTICE PRESENTS' now sits under the headline instead of above it. B is slightly worse because the edge of the planet circle cuts through the SOLSTICE wordmark and makes the logo harder to read, while in A the logo stays clean.

The two candidates are almost pixel-identical; the only difference is that A's SOLSTICE logo is slightly larger than B's, and neither version is clearly better because of it. Both just shrink the square layout onto a taller canvas instead of rearranging it. That leaves about 200px of dead space below the 'Reserve a spot' line, where the only thing is the broken 'missing asset' partner placeholder, which is still visible. The pill badges and the URL line are tiny at this size, the can graphic floats with nothing beside it, and the large planet circle crowds the top-left corner.

Both are nearly identical 320x50 banners. In each, the attribution 'THE SOLSTICE TASTING TEAM' is set in bold caps at the bottom-left, below the quote mark and to the left of the quote, so it outweighs the italic quote and confuses the reading order. The quote text is tiny, and the can is shrunk into an unrecognisable sliver against the right edge. A drops the SOLSTICE logo entirely. B keeps a logo, but as an illegible speck crammed under 'soon.', which only slightly beats losing the brand altogether.

Both use the same skyscraper layout with the same flaws. The attribution 'THE SOLSTICE TASTING TEAM' sits above the quote, which reverses the reading order, and the label is too small to read. The quote breaks into many short lines that end on words like 'a' and 'glass:'. The bottle and circle are shrunk and leave dead space at the bottom. B's SOLSTICE logo is even smaller and fainter than A's and is close to unreadable, so A edges ahead.

Both are the same mostly scaled layout: quote, attribution and can are placed as in the original. Both leave a dead band in the middle left of the canvas, and the can sits off-centre in an enlarged bleed circle, so the layout looks shrunk rather than rearranged for the new shape. The only visible difference is the bottom-left logo. A keeps the original's mixed glyph sizes at a proportional scale. B's logo is oversized and its glyphs look evened out, so its shapes no longer match the original, which makes A slightly more faithful to the brand.

The two candidates look the same: both are the square layout scaled down to 300x250 with no real rearrangement. In both, the 'THE GROVE TASTING TEAM' attribution and the 'SOLSTICE' can label are too small to read, and the can sits jammed against the bottom edge. Under the quote there is a band of dead space while the left half of the canvas is mostly empty. The colours, fonts and quote all survive intact.

Both candidates are effectively the same layout; the only difference is that B's SOLSTICE wordmark is a hair wider. Both share the same flaws: the top ~150px is empty dead space; the two decorative circles have been pulled fully inside the canvas, so they lose the original's edge bleed and the big maroon circle now dominates the lower half. The product can is small and sits off-centre inside it, and the quote, attribution and logo stay in a ragged left column with no clear relationship to the can.

The two candidates are almost pixel-identical; B's logo sits only a few pixels higher than A's. Both are a uniformly shrunk copy of the square with no rearrangement. The large maroon circle now runs up into the end of the quote and the attribution, the 'SOLSTICE' wordmark and the can label are too small to read at 300×250, and the attribution line is tiny. The can is jammed against the bottom edge while the right half above it is empty.

The two layouts are identical, and both have the same flaw: the photo panel no longer fills the canvas height. It sits inset, with dark bands of about 15px above and below while running flush to the right edge, so it looks like a letterboxed leftover rather than a deliberate rearrangement. The left column also leaves extra empty space below the CTA. A breaks the headline better ('Your coffee, / on repeat'), while B keeps the original's awkward break that leaves 'on' dangling at the end of line 1, so A edges it.

A and B look pixel-identical, so this is a tie. Both have the same flaws. The headline reads well left to right on one line, but the 'NEW VIDEO' badge is shrunk until its text is illegible and is crammed under the logo in the left column. 'Full review inside.' wraps into three tiny lines jammed against the right edge, and the shoe-in-circle hero image is reduced to a thumbnail, so key imagery is lost.

A and B look pixel-identical, so this is a tie. Both share the same flaws. The plan cards are shrunk to tiny chips, and the MONTHLY/YEARLY/FAMILY labels and per-month text can't be read. The card order is scrambled to 6, 80, 48, which moves the featured yearly plan out of the middle. The two-line headline nearly touches the top and bottom of the canvas. The subhead and legal text are crammed into a small block against the right edge, and the fine print is close to the subhead's size. The pricing comparison, the core of the message, is effectively lost.

The two candidates look pixel-identical in this 320x50 banner, so neither is better. Both share the same flaws: the price cards are out of order (6, 80, 48, so the dark Yearly card has moved off the centre spot it held as the featured plan), the plan labels and 'per month/year' text are unreadably small, the subtitle is squashed into a tiny three-line block under the logo, and the legal text is a gray smear. The headline and the orange CTA do read clearly and in the right left-to-right order.

The two are almost identical and share the same serious flaws. The headline is a one-word-per-line tower that eats about 60% of the height. The price cards are shrunk to thumbnails with unreadable labels, and they are out of order: Yearly, the featured plan, has moved from the middle to last. The subhead now sits below the CTA, and the fine print is crammed at the bottom. The only difference is the logo: A's is larger and readable, while B's is a tiny centred wordmark that weakens the brand, so A is marginally better.
